# Guidelines and Instructions

This document outlines the structure, deliverables, and evaluation criteria for the upcoming mini-project. Please read all instructions carefully.

## 1. Overview & Timeline

This is a mini-project designed to give you hands-on experience in solving a problem within a team.

## 2. Project Deliverables

Each team is required to submit the following items for evaluation. All items are mandatory.

### A. Source Code in a GitHub Repository

- All code developed for the project must be hosted in a private GitHub repository.
- The repository must be shared with the faculty (and your assigned Teaching Assistants (TAs) if any).
- The repository should include a README file with instructions on how to set up and run your project.

### B. One-Page Write-up

- A concise, two-page summary of your project.
- The write-up should include:
  - Your problem statement
  - The dataset details
  - The approach you took to solve it
  - A brief overview of your implementation
  - Conclusions
- The document must be submitted in PDF format.

## 3. Final Review & Demonstration

- A mandatory review session will be held for all teams. A detailed schedule will be shared by the faculty.
- During the review, each team must present their work using a presentation (slide deck) and give a live demonstration of the working code.
- Be prepared to explain your methodology, code structure, and answer questions from the evaluation panel.

## 4. Evaluation and Marks

- This mini-project carries a total of 10 marks.
- The final grade will be based on:
  - Quality of deliverables
  - Code functionality
  - Repository maintenance
  - Clarity of the write-up
  - Presentation
  - Live demonstration
  - Performance during the Q&A session
  - Individual Contribution
